title: Choose the visual world for the Burlwood website
question: Same hand, reworked to your notes: The Flitch calmed (grain only in the opening, quiet heartwood leaves below) and Walnut & Aluminium worked out as a full hi-fi rack with a working function selector. Neither mentions pre-1.0 or backups. Open each full size from the expand chip and scroll.

options.label: The Flitch
options.lineage: a veneer merchant's sample book: consecutive burl leaves, bookmatched and numbered
options.thesis: A flitch is a log's history cut into numbered leaves, so the page is one: burl veneer drawn in the icon's grain, with the commit lane running through it.
materials: bookmatched burl veneer, drawn as live contour grain
the app set in as a marquetry inlay
options.viewport: 'burl ● wood' split by the HEAD knot over calm bookmatched grain; one line, Download for macOS, the commit graph rising as an inlay. Below, quiet heartwood leaves: history, working tree, the cutting list, install.
options.risk: The literal reading of the name: if the grain is timid or textured like stock wood, it reads as a rustic theme instead of the icon brought to life.

raised.raise: Git meaning is drawn into the grain itself: lanes, forks and the HEAD knot are grain lines, not icons in cards.
Sections are whole leaves of the flitch, numbered in order, never fractional card grids.
Veneer owns whole regions edge to edge; there is no neutral grey page ground.
One fixed reading sweep, leaf 01 to the download leaf, like a cross-check.

options.label: Walnut & Aluminium
options.lineage: 1970s hi-fi catalogues: walnut cabinets around brushed-aluminium faceplates
options.thesis: Burlwood as a hi-fi receiver: a brushed-aluminium faceplate between walnut cheeks, the app behind the dial glass.
materials: rotary selector, pilot lamp, VU meters
options.viewport: The faceplate: the app in a dark dial window with a rotary function selector (Graph · Stage · Diff · Branches) that switches the view; headline, the download as a pilot-lit pushbutton, and Added/Removed meters. Below, stacked units: commits, working tree, specifications, installation.
options.risk: Familiar: retro hi-fi is a well-worn indie Mac app look, and the most likely place this category lands.

options.label: Struck Cathode
options.lineage: nixie decade counters behind bronze anode gauze
options.thesis: Every commit hash present at once as unlit ghosts; HEAD is the one struck forward in orange.
options.viewport: A wall of ghosted 7-character hashes behind gauze; one hash glows, the wordmark and download struck forward beside it.
options.case: Developers know nixie glow and hashes by heart, so it holds identification; it loses clarity because a hash wall says nothing about what the app does.
options.risk: Reads as a novelty clock, not a git client, unless the screenshots carry the explanation.

options.label: Chromatophore Skin
options.lineage: cephalopod skin as a living display
options.thesis: The surface itself changes pattern to signal state.
options.viewport: A pale living surface rippling with patterns.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no developer reads a git client through squid skin, and it hides the product.
options.kept: State drawn into the material itself, not boxed.

options.label: Azulejo Hall
options.thesis: History painted in cobalt across a tile grid.
options.viewport: A framed cobalt panel telling the app's story.
options.case: Fuses poorly: cobalt on white fights the warm graphite app and the wood icon.
options.kept: Layout snaps to whole units, never fractions.

options.label: Solidarity Silkscreen
options.thesis: One emblem, flat fearless fields, a repeating slogan border.
options.viewport: The knot as a centred emblem in hot flat fields.
options.case: Fuses poorly: political-poster urgency is the wrong voice for a calm hobby git client.
options.kept: Colour fields commit to whole regions.

options.label: Night Six-Pack
options.thesis: Six calm gauges cross-checked in a fixed sweep.
options.case: Fuses poorly: gauges want numbers, and there are no benchmarks to show without inventing them.
options.kept: A fixed reading order through the page.

options.label: Chaekgeori Shelf
options.thesis: An inventory cabinet that opens toward you.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an inventory of boxes is the feature grid in costume.
options.kept: No cast shadows; objects are outlined.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What Mac git clients ship (Fork, Tower, GitKraken), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Icon, headline and download centred over a large app screenshot, a feature grid below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
